transcript.content:
hey, i'm berry. whatever your dream was, that's enough to start.

tell it to me however it comes back to you.
ok! the part that keeps coming back is the lift in that old hotel—it had brass walls and a folding metal gate, like really old. i was going up with tomas, my best friend from school.
an old lift with brass walls and that folding gate... that kind stays with you.
yeah exactly. it kept going up for way too long. and when i looked at tomas again he was suddenly about ten, in our old school uniform. he didn't seem to notice at all.
he just went small again, and carried on like nothing was strange.

right. he didn't act any different. and then the lift stopped and the gate opened, but instead of a corridor there was this orchard at dusk. rows of apple trees, every apple glowing softly like a lamp.
out of a lift, into dusk and glowing apples...

yeah, and tomas ran ahead between the trees. there was a white horse standing in the middle of the orchard, very still. it lowered its head so i could touch its nose—it was warm. then tomas was gone and i woke up.
the horse stayed, once tomas was gone.
yeah, the horse was still there when i noticed tomas was gone. i didn't see him leave. then i woke up right after.
just you and the horse, then it was over.
yeah, exactly. just the orchard, the glowing apples, and the horse. then i woke up.
before the horse, and then after you touched its nose?
before the horse, tomas ran ahead into the orchard. after i touched its nose, i looked and he was gone. that's when i woke up.
everything else just faded out, but that moment by the horse is the one that held.
yeah, that's the part that really stuck with me. the horse lowering its head, me touching its nose, how warm it was—that felt the most real.
what's the first thing you remember, before the lift?
i don't remember anything before the lift. it just started with me and tomas already in there, going up.

so it started with you and tomas in that old lift, the brass walls and the folding gate, going up way too long. then tomas was suddenly about ten in your old school uniform, and he didn't notice. the gate opened onto an orchard at dusk, every apple glowing, and tomas ran ahead. there was a white horse standing there, and it lowered its head so you could touch its warm nose. when you looked, tomas was gone, and then you woke up.

did i get it right, or did i miss anything?
you got it right. only thing is the apples were glowing softly like lamps, just to be exact. but yeah, that's the whole thing.

softly, like lamps. i'll remember that.

would you like to see it drawn?
yes, i'd like that.

we could do it as a warm oil painting, soft and warm, gently blurred, as if every edge is melting into the dusk. or a soft pastel drawing, feathery and hazy, with each stroke blending into the next like a half-remembered dream. or an old photograph, still and timeless, with a silver glow that makes every detail feel suspended in memory. or how it really looked to you, vivid and real, yet bathed in that impossible, sourceless light.

does one of those feel closest, or would you describe your own?
the soft pastel drawing feels closest. feathery and hazy, like a half-remembered dream, that's how it felt.

soft pastel, feathery and hazy. i'll start with the lift and the orchard, just as it came to you.

and since you were in it, i'd like to draw you too. would you like me to draw you as you are, or as i imagine you?
as you imagine me is fine. go with your guess.

i'm sketching you and tomas and the white horse and the lift and the orchard at dusk now. everything will appear on the right over the next minute or two. if anything looks wrong once it's there, just say.
it looks right. the lift with the brass walls and folding gate, the orchard at dusk, the glowing apples, tomas in his school uniform, and the white horse—all there.

good, that's what i wanted to check.

does it look the way you remember?
yeah, it looks the way i remember. especially the horse and the glowing apples.

tomas, the white horse, the lift, the orchard at dusk, and you—everyone and everything is in place now. i'll draw the moments of the dream in order, each one carrying on from the one before it, and they'll appear on the right as they're ready.
ok, i'll wait.
they'll be up in a minute or two.
ok.
the lift's up now. the others will follow as i finish them.
ok, i see the lift. looks right.
the next moment's up—tomas suddenly about ten in the old school uniform. does it look the way you remember?
yeah, that's exactly it. he looks just like he did back then, with the uniform and all. he doesn't even seem to notice the change.

tomas looks right to you—good.

i'm sorry, though. two of the moments couldn't be drawn because of a problem on our side—the lift opening onto the orchard, and tomas running ahead between the glowing apple trees. the other two moments are still being drawn and will appear on the right soon.
oh, that's too bad about those two. but thanks for telling me. i'll wait for the other two.

the moment with the white horse in the orchard is up now.

does it look the way you saw it?
yeah, the horse looks right. still, white, in the middle of the trees.
good. the last moment is still being drawn and will appear on the right soon.
ok, i'll keep an eye out.

the last moment's up now—tomas gone, and you looking and he's not there.

does it look the way you remember?
yeah, that's right. tomas isn't in it, and i'm looking around like i just noticed he's gone. that's how it felt.

good, that's how it felt for you.

i'm sorry again that two of the moments couldn't be drawn—the lift opening onto the orchard, and tomas running ahead between the glowing apple trees. four of the six are there on the right. thank you for sharing this dream with me, and you can look through them there.
